title: Register new test commands before the independent validation stage
rationale: The implementation passed its agent-run tests, but the factory's independent validation was skipped because its command source was still empty. Updating that source during documentation was too late for this run's implementation gate.
evidence: runs/20261017-222534/events.jsonl:3459 records validation_skipped with reason "no commands in docs/VALIDATION.md". pi-implement-1.jsonl:446 shows the new unittest suite passing. The documenter only added its executable shell fence afterward, at pi-document-1.jsonl:828–830. run-state.json records approval in loop 1 and no cap exhaustion, so this is a validation-coverage gap rather than an implementation failure.
proposed_change: Add a pre-handoff rule: when introducing or changing a repository test/check command, ensure the factory's existing validation-command source covers it before handing off. With the default docs/VALIDATION.md source, add or update the minimal fast, self-terminating, non-interactive command in an executable sh fence, preserving existing commands and normative requirements. Respect any explicit validation override instead of introducing competing configuration. Run the command and include the registration status in completion evidence; if updating the source is prohibited, report the precise blocker rather than assuming the later documentation stage supplies this run's independent gate.

application.summary: Added a portable pre-handoff validation-command registration rule to agents/implementer.md, including override preservation, safe command requirements, execution evidence, and blocker reporting. Focused validation and lint passed; three full-suite failures were confirmed pre-existing.

title: Put completion evidence inside the structured handoff summary
rationale: The implementer supplied useful validation evidence in prose, but its structured summary retained only a description of the changes. Keeping concise evidence inside the existing summary field makes the persisted handoff useful without requiring transcript inspection or a contract change.
evidence: pi-implement-1.jsonl:864–866 contains a completion-evidence section with the expected initial failure, passing test command, working-directory check, and working-tree review. The JSON summary immediately following it only says a script and regression test were added. events.jsonl:3458 persists that evidence-free summary, while events.jsonl:3459 shows that independent validation was skipped.
proposed_change: Replace the closing handoff instruction with wording that explicitly requires the completion-evidence summary inside the returned JSON object's summary string, not solely in surrounding prose. Preserve the existing requirements for PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED statuses, precise blockers, and whole-working-tree review. Require concise actual commands and observed results, plus acceptance-criterion coverage, without adding new contract fields or repeating the same report outside the JSON.

title: Make the reviewer task explicitly cover affected documentation
rationale: The task template foregrounds only coding standards, narrowing the broader review required by the role prompt. This run passed validation and received approval in one loop, but the reviewer did not inspect the architecture or validation documents that the implementation changed. Making those checks explicit in the task template would strengthen the independent review without requiring extra runtime checks.
evidence: runs/20261017-224544/pi-implement-2.jsonl:34–36 records the reviewer's only file reads: hello.py, tests/test_hello.py, and docs/coding-standards.md. It then approved with no findings in review-1.md. Meanwhile, pi-implement-1.jsonl:749–751 records changes to README.md, docs/architecture.md, and docs/VALIDATION.md. agents/reviewer.md requires reviewing protected-document accuracy, but agents/reviewer.user.md opens by asking only for review against docs/coding-standards.md.
proposed_change: Replace the opening instruction with: 'Review the work against the full plan, applicable repository contracts, and affected documentation—not only coding standards. If your tools include a shell, inspect `git diff {{trunk}}...HEAD`; otherwise review the repository as it stands on this branch. Before approving, read the current architecture and validation guidance and the usage/interface documentation affected by the planned behavior. Verify their relevant statements against the implementation; a plan's description of a document is not evidence of its current contents. Do not defer this accuracy check merely because a later documentation stage exists.' Preserve the existing plan and documentation placeholders and scope instructions.
